vigil_note:
On vigil-ranked feasts such as today, the Typicon’s principal provision is that Great Vespers pass directly into Matins. In this case, if Compline is said, it precedes Great Vespers, according to Athonite practice and the Eye of the Church Typicon; in modern practice, however, it is usually omitted.
If, according to the newer provision, Matins does not follow Great Vespers, no rubric is given for the placement of Compline; if it is not omitted, it may reasonably be said after Great Vespers.
canon_refrain: O most holy Mother of God, save us.
daily_troparia: (Tone 4) God of our fathers, You always treat us fairly.* Deprive us not of Your mercy,** but by their prayers direct our lives in peace.

Clothed as in purple and fine linen* with the blood of Your martyrs throughout the world,* Your Church cries out to You through them, O Christ God:* send down Your loving-kindness on Your people;* grant peace to Your community,** and to our souls great mercy.
(Tone 8, kontakion) With the Saints grant rest, O Christ,* to the souls of Your servants,* where there is neither pain, nor sorrow, nor sighing,** but life everlasting.
Through the prayers of all the saints, and of the Mother of God,* grant us Your peace, O Lord, and have mercy on us,** for You alone are merciful.
saturday_theotokion: O Lord, Master of nature,* the world offers You the godly martyrs as the first-fruits of nature.* By their supplications, through the Mother of God,* preserve Your Church and Your people in profound peace,** O most merciful One.
prayers: O Lady, bride of God, virginal, pure, immaculate, blameless, without stain or disgrace, who through your birth-giving brought together our fallen state and the things of heaven; O you, only hope of the hopeless, help of the oppressed, ready protection of those who flee to you, and refuge of all Christians: do not despise me, a wretched sinner, who have defiled myself with unclean thoughts, words and deeds, and in my slothfulness have become a slave to the passions of life. Since you are the Mother of God, Who is the Lover of mankind, have mercy, have compassion on me a sinner and a prodigal son; accept this prayer from my impure lips, and, with the power of your maternity, beg your Son, our Lord and our God, to open for me the depths of His loving kindness, forgive me my countless sins, convert me to true repentance, and make me faithful to His commands. O you who are compassionate, be my constant companion: in this present life, be with me as an intercessor, as a powerful help to turn away the assaults of the enemies and to guide me to salvation; at the hour of my death, be with me to embrace my poor soul and to keep away the dreadful sight of the wicked devils; on the terrible day of judgment, deliver me from eternal punishment and make me an heir of your Son’s glory, through the grace and the love for mankind of your Son our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him and to His eternal Father, and to His all-holy, good, and life-giving Spirit, is glory, honor, and adoration, now and always and for ever and ever. Amen.

Now that we are about to lie down to sleep, grant us, O Master, the repose of our soul and body. Preserve us against the dark slumber of sin and against any impure sensuality that roams around in the darkness of night; quiet the assaults of our passions, arrest the darts that the Evil One insidiously throws at us, still the rebellions of our flesh, and still all earthly and worldly feeling within us. Grant us, O Lord, a watchful mind, innocent thoughts, a sober heart, a gentle sleep free from evil dreams; at the hour of prayer, arouse us, strong in the practice of Your precepts and ever-mindful of Your desires; give us the grace to sing Your glory throughout the night; to praise, bless and glorify Your all-honorable and magnificent name, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, always, now and for ever and ever. Amen.
O you most glorious, ever-virginal and blessed Mother of God, commend our prayer to your Son, our God, and entreat Him to save our souls through your intercessions.
The Father is my hope, the Son my refuge, the Holy Spirit my protection. O Trinity, one God, glory to You!
penitential_troparia: (Tone 6) Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us:* since we have no defense,* we sinners offer this supplication to You, our Master,** have mercy on us.

Lord, have mercy on us,* for in You we place our hope,* be not exceedingly angry with us nor mindful of our transgressions;* but look upon us even now with mercy and deliver us from our enemies,* for You are our God and we are Your people:** we are all the work of Your hands, and we call upon Your name.

Open to us the doors of mercy, O blessed Mother of God,* that we, who place our trust in you may not perish,* but that through you we be delivered from misfortune;** for you are the salvation of all Christians.

with_priest: Typicon prescribes the following rite of forgiveness to be said in monasteries.

Priest, prostrating or bowing low before the faithful:
Bless me, reverend fathers and brothers, and forgive me, a sinner, whatever offenses I may have committed this day [this night] and all the days of my life by word, deed and thought as well as by all the senses of my soul and body.

Faithful:
May God forgive you, reverend Father.
(faithful also prostrate or bow)
Bless me, reverend father, and forgive me, a sinner, whatever offenses I may have committed this day [this night] and all the days of my life by word, deed and thought as well as by all the senses of my soul and body.

Priest:
May the Lord God by His grace forgive you all your sins and have mercy on you.
without_priest: After the dismissal, the following prayer is said. It might be said in prostration.

Remit, pardon, and forgive our transgressions, voluntary and involuntary, in deed and in word, with knowledge and in ignorance, in thought and in desire, by night and by day, forgive them all, O God, for you are good and love mankind.
The following prayer is prescribed in certain horologions of Kyivan tradition, but our current Typicon does not require it at small compline:
Afterwards the following prayer is said:

O Lord, Lover of mankind, forgive them that hate and wrong us.
Do good to them that do good.
Grant our brethren and kindred and those who are alone whatever they ask for their salvation, and life eternal.
Visit the sick and heal them.
Liberate those in captivity.
Guide those at sea and journey with them that travel.
Recall our captive brothers who share our Orthodox faith, and deliver them from every misfortune.
Have mercy, O Lord, on those who asked us, the unworthy, to pray for them and forgive them.
Have mercy, O Lord, on those that serve us and are kind to us, and grant them whatever they ask for their salvation and life eternal.
DEPARTED Remember also, O Lord, us in our lowliness and meanness, and enlighten our minds with the light of knowledge of Your holy Gospel, and guide us in the way of Your commandments; through the prayers of Your most pure Mother and of all Your saints, for You are blessed unto the ages of ages. Amen.
Remember, O Lord, our fathers and brethren departed before us, and all those who died in the pious faith, and let them dwell where the light of Your face shall visit them.
